mission: Ben arrives on Coruscant roughly half a day after Elya sent the message. The body is not warm-on-the-floor fresh, but the investigation is fresh: access controlled, first reports unfinished, official assumptions still forming. Inspector Cale Dorrin, a GA Justice / Coruscant Security investigator assigned to sensitive old-GAG and political-crime cases, controls the scene and lets Ben in under limits because Elya’s message makes him relevant and Luke has quietly vouched for the urgency. Ben senses Force-trauma and recovers the damaged Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest fragment hidden by Elya’s records instincts, not in an obvious safe.
why_now: Ben arrives half a day after Elya sent the message. The scene is still fresh and still controllable — access locked down, first reports still forming, official assumptions not yet hardened into a closed file. If he is going to recover anything Elya preserved, it has to be now.
conflict: Ben wants to recover the fragment Elya hid and understand what it means. His obstacle is Dorrin, who has legal authority over the scene and will let Ben in only so far as Elya’s message makes him relevant — not as far as Ben’s Force sense says he needs to go. Ben has to work within Dorrin’s limits to get what Elya left.
turning_point: Dorrin’s first records check points toward an old GAG personnel/prosecution trail Ben cannot interpret alone.
closing_hook: Dorrin’s first records check points toward an old GAG personnel/prosecution trail Ben cannot interpret alone.
setting: Coruscant, the third-floor records office at the Coruscant Bureau of Post-Conflict Logistics — roughly twelve hours after Elya's death. GA Justice has secured the scene; Inspector Cale Dorrin of GA Justice controls access. This is the capital whose Senate voted the Jedi Order out; the vacated Coruscant Jedi Temple is visible on the mid-distance skyline through the corridor windows Ben does not look at. Elya's body has been removed but the chair, terminal, and blood smear on the terminal edge remain. Daytime overhead lighting now, harsh and fluorescent. Other Bureau offices on the floor have been cleared for the investigation.

stakes.personal: Ben has to walk into the room where Elya died because of a message she sent him using his old GAG marker. The Force-trauma he senses in the office is precise and wrong in a way he recognizes without wanting to. His wound: he knew this marker still worked; he just told himself he would never have to use it.
stakes.interpersonal: Dorrin gives Ben access on procedural sufferance — Elya’s message makes Ben relevant, Luke’s quiet backing opens the door, but Dorrin is measuring every step. He will close access the moment Ben goes past what the evidence supports. The dynamic is professional friction with stakes: Dorrin’s caution is the law, and Ben needs the law to stay on his side.
stakes.external: The fragment, once recovered, shows a cloned shipment identity under quarantine disguise with Jacen’s personal encryption marker. It is proof that one of Jacen’s last orders had two lives. It is not enough to solve the case — but Dorrin’s first records check begins pointing toward someone who can read what it means.

sensory_details: Harsh daytime fluorescent overhead in the records office — the same room, wrong light. Elya’s chair is still angled toward the terminal; a dark smear on the terminal edge. The air carries the chemical smell of forensic processing. Through a corridor window on his way in, the vacated Jedi Temple catches the mid-morning light on its upper spires — Ben registers it the way you register a word you’ve decided not to say, and does not look at it twice. He notices exits first, then the Force-silence where someone was taken apart with something precise.
canon_elements_needed: GA Justice jurisdiction on Coruscant post-Order-exile — Dorrin operates in the legal vacuum the Senate created
Vacated Coruscant Jedi Temple on the skyline as a wound Ben does not look at
The GA Senate vote expelling the Order — context for why GA Justice controls a crime that touches a Jedi

turning_point_detail.trigger: Dorrin's first records check surfaces Talon Veyr's name — worked under Elya, conviction involving similar manifest/transfer-chain patterns. The fragment alone means nothing; there is a person who can read it.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben has a name, a location (Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works), and a reason — but the legal route to Talon is the only path that does not blow the investigation wide open.
turning_point_detail.cost: Using the legal route means filing the kind of request that wakes old GAG-adjacent alert systems. Ben does not know this yet. He does the responsible thing.

emotional_arc.start: Ben arrives prepared for professional procedure and quietly braced for whatever the Force-residue tells him. He is competent and slightly taut.
emotional_arc.shift: The Force-trauma signature in the office is precise, intimate, and wrong — not a fight, not desperation. Something controlled was done here. He knows the shape of it without being able to name it yet.
emotional_arc.end: He recovers the fragment and lets Dorrin run the records check. He has what Elya saved. He does not yet know what it costs to have asked for it.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben enters Elya's office under Dorrin's access limits — the body is gone but the chair is still angled toward the terminal and there is a dark smear on its edge.
key_beats.state_change: Ben is inside the room where Elya died, with legal sufferance and no margin to exceed it.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Counting exits before anything else — the habit firing before he can stop it; then the Force-silence where a person used to be, wrong and specific in a way he knows without wanting to.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben senses Force-trauma in the room: precise, intimate, controlled — not a fight, not desperation, something systematic done to a person who could not defend against it.
key_beats.state_change: He has a shape for how Elya died — a method, not a random act — and the shape is familiar enough to disturb him.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The recognition arriving before the name for it — the body going still, the pull to step back from the Force-impression because he knows the shape from the inside.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben follows Elya's records instinct rather than an obvious hiding place and recovers the damaged manifest fragment.
key_beats.state_change: The fragment is in evidence; Elya's last act of concealment worked.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The small flat fact of finding the thing — no triumph, just the confirmation that she was good at her job and it mattered.

key_beats.beat_description: Dorrin examines the fragment; neither he nor Ben can decode the Jacen-encrypted GAG marker.
key_beats.state_change: The fragment is evidence of concealment but not yet proof — they need someone who can read what the audit trail means.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The familiar patience of a case that is not done — holding the thing without understanding it yet, which is different from uncertainty.

key_beats.beat_description: Dorrin's records check surfaces Talon Veyr: he worked under Elya after a reassignment and his later conviction involved manifest-authorization patterns close to the recovered fragment.
key_beats.state_change: Ben has a name, a location, and a reason — the person who can read the fragment is in a prison on Tarn Velos.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The forward lean — the case clicking into the next stage; and underneath it, the recognition that he is going to have to explain to Dorrin why he knows GAG authorization chains faster than he should.

notes:
Source: Chapter Outlines v4.1. Act: Act One — The Body / The Prison / The Partnership. Chapter title: Not Well (Inciting Incident).

Reader-facing clarity note: The fragment is not enough to solve the case. It shows a duplicated shipment identity, a quarantine/survey disguise, Jacen’s personal encryption marker, and a partial GAG logistics/audit trace. Dorrin can validate the official case context and preserve access, but he cannot interpret what the fragment means.

Texture thread: The vacated Jedi Temple is a skyline wound — one beat, no dwelling; Ben’s decision not to look at it tells the drafter and reader everything about his relationship to what Coruscant voted for.
